# ADAPTED-SETUP COVERAGE (generated by scripts/adapted-setup-coverage.mjs)

Classification of all 551 canonical exercises: which
supported contexts materially change THIS exercise's setup (strap/
cuff, one-arm same-station, seated same-equipment, supported,
reduced range), versus rows where the adaptation is a different
library exercise or no setup change exists. The classifier lives
ONCE in src/lib/exercise/adaptedSetup.js (materialContextsFor) and
is what the exercise screen renders from: class-level default text
per context (GC-D11) with the richer per-exercise entries
overriding it. The split follows GC-D9: setup text only where the
SAME exercise changes setup; different-exercise adaptations live in
the library and are routed by eligibility and swaps.

## Headline

- Materially need adapted-setup text: **220** of 551 exercises (40%)
- Context needs across those rows: **308** (an exercise can need several)
- Resolved by a rich per-exercise entry: **18**
- Resolved by the class default line: **290**
- Unresolved: **0** (coverage of the materially-needing set: 100%)
- Exercises carrying a rich entry: 16 of 220 needing rows (plus enrichment entries below)

## Needs by context

- strap_cuff: 121 exercises
- seated: 72 exercises
- one_arm: 64 exercises
- supported: 37 exercises
- reduced_range: 14 exercises

## Rows needing no adapted-setup text (331), by reason

- 92: no supported context changes this setup; base instructions suffice
- 71: already seated/supported by design
- 58: machine station is inherently seated/supported; its own adjustments are the setup (flagship stations carry wheelchair-positioning text as enrichment)
- 50: floor class: floor-access eligibility and library variants govern
- 18: free-implement isolation usable from any base without setup change
- 16: machine arm/leg independence varies per model; adaptation guidance would be per-gym, not per-exercise
- 16: inherently single-sided; the per-side nature is the exercise itself
- 8: impact class: eligibility, not setup, governs
- 2: hand-loading class: the weight-through-hands axis and library variants govern

## Recorded boundary (not a gap)

Machine one-arm/one-leg use depends on whether the specific gym's
station has independent arms, converging handles or a fixed yoke -
per-model knowledge no exercise database can honestly claim. The
picker's capability questions and per-user allowances carry those
cases; flagship machine stations carry wheelchair-positioning text
as enrichment entries.
